title: PPF Training Handbook — Study Set
subtitle: Parts 1–3: Foundations, Installation Workflow, Customer Lifecycle

questions.handoutTitle: PPF Materials, Top Coats, and Ceramic Layers
questions.q: Which base polymer is the gold standard for modern PPF and the only family that supports genuine self-healing top coats?
options: PVC
TPH
TPU
Polyolefin
questions.why: TPU is highly elastic, has excellent clarity, and is the only family that supports genuine self-healing. PVC is yesterday's material; TPH is a budget blend. (1.1 §1)

questions.handoutTitle: PPF Materials, Top Coats, and Ceramic Layers
questions.q: What is TPH film?
options: Pure aliphatic TPU with a thicker top coat
A blend of TPU with cheaper polymers to bring the price down
A heat-activated ceramic film
PVC with a self-healing additive
questions.why: TPH (thermoplastic polyurethane hybrid) blends TPU with cheaper polymers. It sits a clear step below TPU on every measurable property. (1.1 §1)

questions.handoutTitle: PPF Materials, Top Coats, and Ceramic Layers
questions.q: Which type of TPU stays clear under UV and is used for the top, sun-facing cap layer of a good film?
options: Aromatic TPU
Plasticised PVC
Polyolefin hybrid
Aliphatic TPU
questions.why: Aliphatic TPU has no aromatic rings to form yellow chromophores under UV, so it stays clear. Aromatic TPU yellows and is used only in non-UV-exposed inner layers. (1.1 §2)

questions.handoutTitle: PPF Materials, Top Coats, and Ceramic Layers
questions.q: A customer's white car shows a yellow tint visible through the film, worst near the headlights and lower bumper. Which cause does this point to?
options: Adhesive yellowing accelerated by heat
UV degradation of an aromatic top layer
Trapped iron contamination from prep
Top-coat oxidation from a hot wash
questions.why: Adhesive yellowing shows as a tint visible through the film, especially under heat (bonnet, headlights, lower bumper), and is most obvious on white paint. (1.1 §3)

questions.handoutTitle: PPF Materials, Top Coats, and Ceramic Layers
questions.q: Heat-activated (standard) self-healing top coats typically need roughly what surface temperature before a scratch recovers?
options: Above 40–50°C
Above 0°C
Above 15–25°C (ambient room temperature)
Above 100°C
questions.why: Standard heat-activated coats only become mobile enough to heal above roughly 40–50°C — sun, a hot wash, or a heat gun. Room-temperature coats heal at 15–25°C. (1.1 §4)

questions.handoutTitle: PPF Materials, Top Coats, and Ceramic Layers
questions.q: Why should you never apply a generic, paint-grade ceramic coating over PPF?
options: It makes the film too hydrophobic to wash
It permanently voids the film's self-healing instantly
It reacts with the slip solution and discolours
It cures hard and glassy, so it cracks, hazes, or delaminates as the film flexes
questions.why: Generic coatings cure to a rigid layer that can't flex with the film; as the PPF moves it cracks or delaminates. Use a coating formulated specifically for PPF. (1.1 §5)

questions.handoutTitle: PPF Adhesives — How They Work and How They Fail
questions.q: Almost every modern PPF uses which adhesive chemistry?
options: Silicone PSA
Epoxy resin
Pressure-sensitive acrylic copolymer
Rubber-based hot melt
questions.why: Modern PPF uses a pressure-sensitive acrylic copolymer — clear, UV-stable, and tunable to the exact tack profile needed. (1.2 §2)

questions.handoutTitle: PPF Adhesives — How They Work and How They Fail
questions.q: What is the main job of slip solution?
options: To speed up tack development at the edges
To lower surface tension so the film can be positioned before it grabs
To degrease the panel before install
To harden the adhesive permanently
questions.why: Slip solution (water plus a little surfactant) lowers surface tension and stops the adhesive grabbing until you commit to a position. Tack solution does the opposite. (1.2 §3)

questions.handoutTitle: PPF Adhesives — How They Work and How They Fail
questions.q: Tack solution is water plus what, used to accelerate bonding at edges?
options: A higher dose of baby shampoo
Distilled vinegar
Iron remover
A small percentage of isopropyl alcohol (typically 10–25%)
questions.why: Tack solution is water plus roughly 10–25% IPA. The alcohol flashes off and displaces slip, leaving the adhesive in clean contact with the paint. (1.2 §3)

questions.handoutTitle: PPF Adhesives — How They Work and How They Fail
questions.q: Full cure of PPF adhesive — rated peel strength and complete moisture flash-off — takes about how long?
options: 24 hours
30 days
7 days
6 months
questions.why: Initial bond is ~24 hours, working bond ~7 days, full cure ~30 days. A bubble still present at 30 days is contamination or a defect, not water. (1.2 §4)

questions.handoutTitle: PPF Adhesives — How They Work and How They Fail
questions.q: When removing film at end of life, what is the safest approach?
options: Pull cold at a 90° angle for a clean tear
Soak in acetone first to dissolve the adhesive
Heat the film to about 60–70°C and pull slowly at a low angle
Use a zero-degree pressure washer to lift the edge
questions.why: Heat softens the adhesive (~60–70°C, lower than the 80–90°C post-heat); pull slow and at a low angle. Moist heat — steam or hot demineralised water — is the gentler option. Pulling cold or at 90° raises the risk of taking clear coat with it. (1.2 §6, 2.6 §3)

questions.handoutTitle: Matt and Gloss PPF — Surfaces, GU Matching, and Install Differences
questions.q: What gives gloss film its mirror-like quality at the surface?
options: A molecularly smooth top coat producing specular reflection
Matting agents scattering light internally
Micro-texturing that diffuses light
A thicker aliphatic cap layer
questions.why: Gloss is polished TPU — a molecularly smooth surface reflects light in one direction (specular reflection). Matt scatters light (diffuse reflection). (1.3 §1)

questions.handoutTitle: Matt and Gloss PPF — Surfaces, GU Matching, and Install Differences
questions.q: What happens if a matt top coat self-heals fully back to its original state?
options: The film permanently yellows
The healed area turns locally glossy because the texture is smoothed out
The adhesive releases at that spot
Nothing visible changes
questions.why: Full recovery smooths the micro-texture, so the matt finish goes locally glossy. This is why matt self-healing is handled differently by manufacturers. (1.3 §2)

questions.handoutTitle: Matt and Gloss PPF — Surfaces, GU Matching, and Install Differences
questions.q: Which gloss-meter angle is the universal reference you report on every measurement as a baseline?
questions.why: 60° is the universal reference. Use 20° for high gloss (60° reading above 70 GU) and 85° for low-gloss/matt (60° reading below 10 GU). (1.3 §3)

questions.handoutTitle: Matt and Gloss PPF — Surfaces, GU Matching, and Install Differences
questions.q: For a matt-on-matt partial install, what GU difference is effectively invisible at the relevant angle?
options: Within 3–5 GU
Within 6–8 GU
Up to 10 GU
Within 1–2 GU
questions.why: Within 1–2 GU is invisible; 3–5 GU is visible up close; more than 5 GU is visible from across the street. (1.3 §4)

questions.handoutTitle: Matt and Gloss PPF — Surfaces, GU Matching, and Install Differences
questions.q: Why should you wrap a squeegee blade in a fresh microfibre or felt sleeve on matt film?
options: To avoid burnishing the matt surface into gloss
To apply more pressure
To keep slip solution off the film
To warm the film faster
questions.why: Bare hard plastic burnishes matt into locally glossy spots that don't recover. A sleeve protects the texture — and is changed regularly so grit doesn't sand the film. (1.3 §5)

questions.handoutTitle: Matt and Gloss PPF — Surfaces, GU Matching, and Install Differences
questions.q: Which is a correct aftercare rule for matt PPF you give the customer?
options: Carnauba wax restores the matt look
Automatic brush washes are fine once a month
pH-neutral shampoo only, no wax or conventional sealants
Drag-dry with a towel to avoid streaks
questions.why: Matt needs pH-neutral shampoo, no carnauba/sealants/quick detailers, hand wash only (brushes burnish it), and pat-dry rather than drag. (1.3 §6)

questions.handoutTitle: Van der Waals Adhesion — Why Surface Prep Matters
questions.q: What actually holds PPF on the paint, according to this handout?
options: A chemical glue that bonds to the clear coat
Suction created by the squeegee
Static electricity from the film
Van der Waals forces — molecular attraction across the contact zone
questions.why: The film is held by trillions of weak Van der Waals forces between molecules — not glue. The adhesive's job is to get molecularly close to the paint. (1.4)

questions.handoutTitle: Van der Waals Adhesion — Why Surface Prep Matters
questions.q: Van der Waals forces only work when two surfaces are within about how far apart?
options: 1 nanometre
1 millimetre
1 micrometre
1 centimetre
questions.why: They are extremely short-range — about 1 nanometre, roughly 1/100,000 the thickness of a human hair. Any contaminant creates a gap and kills the bond. (1.4)

questions.handoutTitle: Van der Waals Adhesion — Why Surface Prep Matters
questions.q: Why is water alone not enough as a final prep step before film?
options: It leaves mineral spots
It does not remove oils — you need a degreaser or IPA wipe
It activates the adhesive too early
It cools the panel below working temperature
questions.why: Water doesn't remove oils. The final pass must be a degreaser (IPA or panel wipe) to create a molecularly clean surface. (1.4)

questions.handoutTitle: Van der Waals Adhesion — Why Surface Prep Matters
questions.q: Which analogy does the handout use to explain how PPF grips with no glue?
options: A magnet on a fridge
Velcro hooks and loops
A suction cup on glass
A gecko walking on a ceiling
questions.why: A gecko grips using only Van der Waals forces via millions of microscopic foot hairs that get close enough to the surface. PPF adhesive works the same way. (1.4)

questions.handoutTitle: Water Goes, Air Stays — The Science of Bubbles Under Fresh PPF
questions.q: Why does water trapped under fresh film clear itself but trapped air does not?
options: Water is lighter than air
Water can dissolve into the film and pass through as vapour; air cannot
Air evaporates faster than water
The adhesive absorbs air but repels water
questions.why: Water dissolves into the TPU and travels through as vapour, then evaporates off the top. Air barely dissolves and has no path or push, so it just sits there. (1.5)

questions.handoutTitle: Water Goes, Air Stays — The Science of Bubbles Under Fresh PPF
questions.q: On the bench, which appearance is most likely trapped air rather than water?
options: A discrete pocket that does not shrink at all
A fine misty haze over an area that fades day by day
A small domed pocket that shrinks a little each day
A speck at the centre of the pocket
questions.why: Haze and shrinking pockets are water; a discrete pocket that doesn't shrink is trapped air; a central speck is contamination. (1.5 diagnosis table)

questions.handoutTitle: Water Goes, Air Stays — The Science of Bubbles Under Fresh PPF
questions.q: What is the correct way to deal with a trapped air pocket?
options: Leave it — it will clear within a week like water
Park the car in a humid garage to soften it
Work it out by hand on the day: squeegee to the edge, heat and re-press
Wait 30 days for it to flash off
questions.why: Air has no self-clearing route. Work it to the nearest edge with firm strokes, add heat and re-press, pin-prick at the edge only as a last resort — all on the day. (1.5)

questions.handoutTitle: Water Goes, Air Stays — The Science of Bubbles Under Fresh PPF
questions.q: Which conditions make trapped water clear fastest?
options: Warm, dry, sunny
Cold, damp, shaded
Cool and humid
Freezing and still
questions.why: Warm, dry, sunny air pulls water out faster and speeds it through the film. A car in a humid garage clears slowest. Proper install temp is min 20°C, sweet spot 22–25°C. (1.5)

questions.handoutTitle: Water Goes, Air Stays — The Science of Bubbles Under Fresh PPF
questions.q: In the permeation equation P = D × S, why does water permeate the film so much better than oxygen or nitrogen?
options: Water molecules are far smaller than gas molecules
Water wins on solubility — it is polar and hydrogen-bonds into the polar TPU and adhesive
Gases are blocked by the top coat entirely
Water is pushed by gravity through the film
questions.why: Permeability = diffusivity × solubility. Water is polar and hydrogen-bonds into the TPU and acrylic, so it dissolves in readily; non-polar gases have near-zero solubility despite similar molecule size. (1.5)

questions.handoutTitle: SOP — Vehicle Intake and Inspection
questions.q: What are the four specific purposes of an intake?
options: Greet, upsell, schedule, invoice
Wash, decontaminate, polish, degrease
Quote, deposit, book, confirm
Establish condition, identify anything affecting the work, set expectations, create a paper trail
questions.why: Intake exists to record exact arrival condition, flag anything affecting the work, set customer expectations, and create a protective paper trail. (2.1 §1)

questions.handoutTitle: SOP — Vehicle Intake and Inspection
questions.q: The walk-around should be done how?
options: Whatever order suits the day
Only when the customer reports a problem
In the same order every time, on every vehicle, to build a habit that doesn't skip steps
By the customer, who knows the car best
questions.why: Consistency is the point — same order every time so steps aren't skipped when you're tired or busy. The installer inspects; the customer confirms. (2.1 §3, §6)

questions.handoutTitle: SOP — Vehicle Intake and Inspection
questions.q: What is the minimum number of photos the SOP sets for documenting a vehicle at intake?
questions.why: A minimum of 12 photos: all four corners, both sides, front, rear, roof, bonnet, boot, and interior — plus close-ups of every defect with a scale reference. (2.1 §3)

questions.handoutTitle: SOP — Vehicle Intake and Inspection
questions.q: Which is proper defect documentation?
options: "Some scratches on driver side"
"Customer says it's fine"
"Three light scratches, 5–10cm long, on lower driver's door panel — see photo 7"
"Minor marks here and there"
questions.why: Vague descriptions aren't documentation. Specifics with size, location and a photo reference are. (2.1 §6)

questions.handoutTitle: SOP — Vehicle Intake and Inspection
questions.q: A customer mentions they'd like to add mirror caps, but it isn't on the signed form. What does the SOP say?
options: If it isn't on the signed form, it isn't in the job — add, sign and price it, or don't do it
Do it as a free goodwill extra
Add it verbally and sort the paperwork later
Refuse all scope changes once booked
questions.why: Verbal scope agreements aren't a scope. Either add it, sign it, and price it — or don't do it. Ambiguity is where disputes start. (2.1 §6)

questions.handoutTitle: SOP — Surface Prep and Decontamination
questions.q: According to the SOP, what is the single biggest determinant of how an install looks at 1, 3, and 7 years?
options: The film brand
The installer's hand skill during application
The ambient humidity
The prep
questions.why: Not the film, brand, or hand skill — the prep. Film on a contaminated surface lifts and traps contamination permanently. (2.2 intro)

questions.handoutTitle: SOP — Surface Prep and Decontamination
questions.q: Which prep stage is described as the single most common prep failure when skipped?
options: Initial wash
Clay (or clay-equivalent)
Iron remover
Air blow-down
questions.why: Clay removes bonded contaminants that survive iron and tar removers; skipping it is the most common prep failure. (2.2 §2, §6)

questions.handoutTitle: SOP — Surface Prep and Decontamination
questions.q: What is the last thing that should touch the paint before the film?
options: An IPA-based panel-wipe / dedicated PPF prep solution
A wax sealant
Slip solution
A clay bar
questions.why: Stage 6 is the final wipe with an IPA-based panel prep solution over every panel that will receive film, in straight overlapping passes. (2.2 §2)

questions.handoutTitle: SOP — Surface Prep and Decontamination
questions.q: Freshly repainted panels should generally not be filmed until the paint has cured for roughly how long?
options: 24 hours
7 days
30 days at room temperature (longer in cold)
1 year
questions.why: Fresh paint must be fully cured — typically 30 days at room temperature, longer in cold. Film over uncured paint can lift solvents and damage the finish. (2.2 §3)

questions.handoutTitle: SOP — Surface Prep and Decontamination
questions.q: In the water sheet test, what does beading after a light mist indicate?
options: The panel is perfectly prepped
Silicone contamination
The panel is too cold
Residual wax or sealant still on the panel
questions.why: Water should sheet evenly. Beading means residual wax or sealant; fish-eyes mean silicone. Either means more prep is needed. (2.2 §5)

questions.handoutTitle: SOP — Surface Prep and Decontamination
questions.q: What does the SOP recommend about who does the prep?
options: It's ideal apprentice work
Anyone available — prep doesn't affect quality
The most experienced person should do it, or at least verify it
It can be skipped on new cars
questions.why: Prep is the most determinative work in the install. Treating it as junior work means prep quality follows. The most experienced person does or verifies it. (2.2 §6)

questions.handoutTitle: SOP — Full-Front PPF Installation
questions.q: In the fixed full-front panel sequence, which panel is installed last and why?
options: Headlights, because they're fiddly
The front bumper, because the wing edges tuck behind its edge and it is the largest, most complex piece
Mirror caps, because they need the most heat
The bonnet, because it overlaps onto wing and bumper edges already in place
questions.why: Order: bonnet first, then mirror caps, headlights, wings, and the front bumper last. The bumper comes after the wings so the wing edges tuck cleanly behind the bumper edge. The bonnet goes FIRST, not last — it is left open for access to the bumper and wings, its edges get time to dry, and slip solution cannot run down onto panels that already carry film. (2.3 §2)

questions.handoutTitle: SOP — Full-Front PPF Installation
questions.q: How should panel temperature be checked before applying film?
options: By feeling the panel with the back of the hand
With an IR thermometer on every panel
By the shop's ambient thermostat
It doesn't need checking if the bay is warm
questions.why: The IR thermometer verifies panel temperature on every panel — hot panels shorten working time dramatically; you don't judge by hand. (2.3 §3)

questions.handoutTitle: SOP — Full-Front PPF Installation
questions.q: The industry standard for serious shops is to avoid blade work on the vehicle by doing what?
options: Using plotter-cut patterns wherever possible
Free-handing every cut quickly
Cutting only with dull blades for safety
Never trimming film at all
questions.why: Plotter-cut patterns avoid blade contact with paint — every cut on a vehicle risks the paint underneath. Cutting on the car is the exception, not the routine. (2.3 §5)

questions.handoutTitle: SOP — Full-Front PPF Installation
questions.q: When you must cut on the vehicle, which rule applies?
options: Use a dull blade so it can't dig in
Use a fresh blade and minimal pressure, every cut
Press firmly for a clean single pass
Cut free-hand for speed
questions.why: Fresh blade every cut, minimal pressure (blade rides the surface), a guide where possible, cut on a tape line, and document the cut location. (2.3 §5)

questions.handoutTitle: SOP — Full-Front PPF Installation
questions.q: Why must the heat gun be kept moving constantly during edge work?
options: To dry the slip solution faster
To keep the installer's hand cool
To activate the slip solution
Because a stationary gun permanently changes the film's behaviour in that spot — damage that shows up later
questions.why: Overheated film loses its memory and won't hold a wrap; heat held in one spot causes damage that isn't visible until later. The gun is a precision tool, not a hairdryer. (2.3 §4, §7)

questions.handoutTitle: SOP — Full-Front PPF Installation
questions.q: Why is the vehicle not delivered to the customer immediately after install?
options: Adhesive continues to bond for roughly 24–72 hours; delivering early turns lift problems into callbacks
To allow time to invoice
The film needs to be re-cut
To let the paint cure
questions.why: Cure continues 24–72 hours depending on film and conditions; the car waits the minimum cure time. Tell the customer the cure time at booking so the wait isn't a surprise. (2.3 §6, §7)

questions.handoutTitle: SOP — Post-Heating: Surface Temperature and Technique
questions.q: What is the target SURFACE temperature window for post-heating, measured at the film?
questions.why: Bring the film surface to 80–90°C measured at the film. Below roughly 70°C the adhesive won't flow reliably; keep it under about 90°C sustained (brief, local peaks to ~100°C are the ceiling). (2.4 §2)

questions.handoutTitle: SOP — Post-Heating: Surface Temperature and Technique
questions.q: What two things happen together in the 80–90°C post-heating band?
options: The slip solution boils off and the film shrinks
The adhesive crystallises and the top coat hardens
The acrylic PSA wets out into the lacquer and the TPU relaxes to accept a new memory
The film bleaches and the bond weakens
questions.why: The PSA softens and flows into the micro-texture to build contact area, while the TPU relaxes and takes a new memory so a wrapped edge holds. The bond sets as the film cools. (2.4 §3)

questions.handoutTitle: SOP — Post-Heating: Surface Temperature and Technique
questions.q: Which areas should the post-heat pass target?
options: Edges, recesses and curves only — not the flat field
The entire panel including the flat field
Only the centre of each panel
Only areas with visible bubbles
questions.why: Work brief and local: post-heat edges, recesses and curves only. Flat field area does not need a post-heat pass. (2.4 §4)

questions.handoutTitle: SOP — Post-Heating: Surface Temperature and Technique
questions.q: What is the safety limit beyond which you risk permanent film distortion and clear-coat damage?
options: Anything above 40°C
Anything above the self-healing range (50–60°C)
There is no upper limit if the gun keeps moving
Sustained above 90°C, or brief local spikes beyond about 100°C
questions.why: Sustained surface temp above 90°C, or brief local spikes beyond about 100°C, risks distortion and clear-coat damage. Hot gun air can be 200°C+, so distance and dwell matter, not the dial. (2.4 §5)

questions.handoutTitle: SOP — Post-Heating: Surface Temperature and Technique
questions.q: How should you verify the surface temperature during post-heating?
options: Trust the heat gun's dial setting
Use an infrared thermometer to spot-check the film mid-pass
Touch the film with a gloved finger
Watch for the film to start to shine
questions.why: Confirm with an IR thermometer, not the gun's setting — the air can read 200°C+ while the film sits at ~80°C. The gap depends on distance and dwell. (2.4 §6)

questions.handoutTitle: SOP — Post-Install QC and Customer Handoff
questions.q: What is the correct relationship between internal QC and the customer handoff?
options: They happen together so the customer sees the inspection
QC is done first by the shop; the handoff happens after QC is completed and signed off
QC is optional if the installer is experienced
The customer performs QC at collection
questions.why: Internal QC is where you find problems — before the customer is contacted. The handoff happens with the customer present, after QC is verified and signed off. (2.5 §1)

questions.handoutTitle: SOP — Post-Install QC and Customer Handoff
questions.q: During QC, who should ideally perform the inspection?
options: A second pair of eyes, not the installer alone
The installer alone, who knows the work best
The customer
Whoever is least busy
questions.why: QC should not be the installer alone — a second pair of eyes catches what the installer's own eyes have stopped noticing. (2.5 §3)

questions.handoutTitle: SOP — Post-Install QC and Customer Handoff
questions.q: At QC, how are air bubbles (as opposed to small water bubbles) treated?
options: Normal at any stage, leave them
Normal up to 30 days
Not normal at any stage — they indicate a bonding problem
Only a concern on matt film
questions.why: Small water bubbles are normal in the first 24–48 hours; air bubbles are not normal at any stage and indicate a bonding problem. (2.5 §2)

questions.handoutTitle: SOP — Post-Install QC and Customer Handoff
questions.q: When does payment and final paperwork happen in the handoff structure?
options: Before the walk-around, to save time
Only by email the next day
Whenever the customer arrives
After the walk-around and the care conversation, not before
questions.why: Payment and paperwork come after the walk-around and the conversation — the customer is paying for a service they have just had explained, not rushing through paperwork first. (2.5 §4)

questions.handoutTitle: SOP — Post-Install QC and Customer Handoff
questions.q: What follow-up rhythm does the SOP build into every project?
options: A single call after 6 months
Only when the customer complains
24–48 hours, then a mandatory in-person check at 2–4 weeks
A check every day for the first week
questions.why: A short message at 24–48 hours, then one mandatory in-person check at 2–4 weeks: free, it includes the first detox wash, and it is required to keep the guarantee valid. (2.5 §6)

questions.handoutTitle: Panel Stretch Guide
questions.q: Which is one of the Five Universal Stretch Principles?
options: Stretch extra 'just in case' for a tighter fit
The squeegee works against the stretch direction
Heat is optional if the stretch looks good
Work your tension wet, at the panel — tension can be redistributed while the film floats on slip
questions.why: Stretch only what the panel demands, work tension wet at the panel (PPF is a wet install — shaping the film in the air before lay-down is vinyl technique), heat sets stretch permanently, relief cuts release tension not edges, and the squeegee follows the stretch direction. (2.8 five principles)

questions.handoutTitle: Panel Stretch Guide
questions.q: Why can an install look perfect on the day yet fail two weeks later, even with a good adhesive bond?
options: The stretch was not set with heat, so elastic memory pulls the film back
The slip solution was too thick
The film was the wrong colour
The customer washed it too gently
questions.why: Stretched film has elastic memory; without heat to set the chains in their new position it slowly returns to shape, pulling edges and lifting corners. No heat = no permanent install. (2.8 Stretch vs Memory)

questions.handoutTitle: Panel Stretch Guide
questions.q: Which panel does the guide rate as the highest-difficulty 'very high' stretch panel — to be trained last?
options: Bonnet
Mirror caps
Wings
Door cups
questions.why: Mirror caps are the smallest panel but need the most stretch with compound curves and almost no flat zone — difficulty 'very high', trained last (Day 11+). (2.8 §4, training progression)

questions.handoutTitle: Panel Stretch Guide
questions.q: On a wheel arch, the film should be handled how?
options: Bridged across the arch in one motion
Wrapped only after the car is delivered
Stretched into the arch (following the curve), not over/across it, working in small sections
Left unwrapped to avoid lifting
questions.why: Stretch into the arch, not over it — the film follows the curve as you push it in, worked in 5–10 cm sections with relief cuts at the 12 and 6 o'clock positions. (2.8 §3 Wings)

questions.handoutTitle: Panel Stretch Guide
questions.q: Stretch marks (cloudy/whitened areas) on a panel most often come from what?
options: Too much post-heat
Too much slip solution
A dull blade
Cold, stiff film stretched too aggressively over a tight radius
questions.why: Across panels, stretch marks trace to cold, stiff film stretched too aggressively over a tight radius. The fix is to bring the film and panel up to working temperature, relax it with steam or hot demineralised water if needed, and reduce how much you stretch in one go. (2.8 failure tables)

questions.handoutTitle: Panel Stretch Guide
questions.q: The guide says every panel failure traces back to one of which four root causes?
options: Brand, batch, weather, luck
Surface prep, over-stretch, no post-heat, slip/technique
Heat, light, dust, water
Blade, squeegee, gun, template
questions.why: "The film didn't fail. The bond did. And the bond is either prep, stretch, heat, or slip." The four universal root causes are surface prep, over-stretch, no post-heat, and slip/technique. (2.8 universal failure modes)

questions.handoutTitle: Lifting Edges Troubleshooting Decision Tree
questions.q: Lifting edges almost always come from one of which four root causes?
options: Stretch, surface prep, activation (no post-heat), slip/technique
Brand, batch, climate, age
Heat, cold, water, oil
Blade, gun, squeegee, tape
questions.why: The four causes are stretch (memory pull-back), surface prep (contamination), activation (no post-heat), and slip/technique. (2.9 Four Causes)

questions.handoutTitle: Lifting Edges Troubleshooting Decision Tree
questions.q: The first diagnostic question (Q1) asks whether the lifting appeared within 24 hours. What does a 'YES' point toward?
options: A stretch or tack problem (memory pull-back or weak initial bond)
A surface prep or activation problem
A film manufacturing defect
Customer abuse
questions.why: Lifting within 24 hours points to stretch/tack; lifting that appears later points to surface prep or activation (a bond that never formed properly). (2.9 Q1)

questions.handoutTitle: Lifting Edges Troubleshooting Decision Tree
questions.q: An edge peels back when touched, with no wrinkling. What does the quick-reference table attribute this to?
options: Over-stretch
Trapped slip solution
Bond never formed — a prep failure (start over with proper degrease)
No post-heat
questions.why: Edge peels back when touched, no wrinkling = bond never formed (prep failure). First action: remove and start over with a proper degrease. (2.9 symptom table)

questions.handoutTitle: Lifting Edges Troubleshooting Decision Tree
questions.q: Lifting with visible cloudiness underneath the film usually means what?
options: Over-stretch
Trapped slip solution — re-squeegee out or replace the section
No post-heat
Contamination
questions.why: Cloudiness underneath indicates trapped slip solution; first action is to re-squeegee it out or replace the section. (2.9 symptom table)

questions.handoutTitle: Lifting Edges Troubleshooting Decision Tree
questions.q: Why do slip solution and water fail as the final wipe before film?
options: They are too cold
They activate tack too early
They leave mineral spots only
They do not remove oils, so the adhesive bonds to a contaminated surface
questions.why: Slip solution and water don't remove oils — the last wipe before film must be a degreaser (IPA/panel wipe), every time. (2.9 Q5)

questions.handoutTitle: The Handover — Returning the Car the Right Way
questions.q: What is the core idea the handover guide is built on?
options: Customers can accurately judge install quality
The cheapest handover wins referrals
Customers can't judge the installation quality — they judge the experience of receiving it
Paperwork matters more than the walk-around
questions.why: Customers can't judge edge wrapping or prep; they judge how it felt to be handed back the keys. That experience decides referrals. (3.1 §1)

questions.handoutTitle: The Handover — Returning the Car the Right Way
questions.q: A customer points at a small mark and asks 'what's that?'. What is the right move?
options: Say you can't see anything
Change the subject to the paperwork
Offer an immediate discount
Acknowledge what they're seeing, explain it honestly, and tell them what happens next
questions.why: Validate what they see (never deny it), explain in plain terms what it is, and give a path forward — it resolves on its own or is addressed at the check-up. (3.1 §4)

questions.handoutTitle: The Handover — Returning the Car the Right Way
questions.q: How should the post-installation check-up be handled at handover?
options: Tell the customer to ring up in a few weeks
Book the appointment then and there, before they leave
Leave it for the customer to decide
Only mention it if a problem appears
questions.why: Book it now — "give us a ring" doesn't happen. A customer who leaves with the appointment booked is far more likely to attend, and it's a warranty condition. (3.1 §3 Step 5)

questions.handoutTitle: The Handover — Returning the Car the Right Way
questions.q: How does the guide describe the value split between the work and the handover?
options: The first 95% of the job earns the customer's money; the last 5% (the handover) earns the next customer's money
The handover is just admin at the end
The handover is 50% of the job
The walk-around is optional for repeat customers
questions.why: A referral from a great handover costs nothing; a paid-ad customer costs hundreds. The last 5% earns the next customer's money. (3.1 §1)

questions.handoutTitle: The Handover — Returning the Car the Right Way
questions.q: A customer asks you to 'just touch up' a small extra job for free at handover. What's the recommended response?
options: Always do it free to build goodwill
Always refuse — extras are never free
Tell them to book a separate appointment and quote later only
Offer to look and price it; a tiny goodwill gesture is fine occasionally, but substantial extra work deserves to be paid for
questions.why: Saying yes for free trains customers that extras are gifts. Look, price it; a small 15-minute thank-you is fine occasionally, bigger work gets a fair quote. (3.1 §4)

questions.handoutTitle: PPF Customer Expectations Guide
questions.q: What does the guide stress PPF actually stands for, to set expectations?
options: Paint PROTECTION Film, not Paint PERFECTION Film
Paint Perfection Film
Permanent Paint Finish
Pristine Paint Forever
questions.why: PPF is Paint PROTECTION Film, not Paint PERFECTION Film — a sacrificial layer that absorbs damage, not a way to make paint flawless. (3.2 Foreword)

questions.handoutTitle: PPF Customer Expectations Guide
questions.q: Where did PPF technology originally come from?
options: Formula 1 in the 1990s
The aerospace coatings industry
1960s US military 'helicopter tape' to protect rotor blades from erosion
Marine boat-wrap film
questions.why: It was developed by 3M for the US military in the Vietnam era to protect helicopter rotor blades — known as "helicopter tape" — before reaching motorsport and then cars. (3.2 Foreword)

questions.handoutTitle: PPF Customer Expectations Guide
questions.q: How does the guide tell customers to distinguish air bubbles from water bubbles?
options: Air bubbles are soft and hazy; water bubbles are sharp
Air bubbles are sharply defined, round, and stay the same size; water bubbles are soft/cloudy and shrink and disappear
Both clear within 24 hours
Air bubbles only appear on matt film
questions.why: Water bubbles are soft, cloudy and evaporate over 7–14 days; air bubbles are sharply defined, round and don't disappear on their own. (3.2 Air/Water bubbles)

questions.handoutTitle: PPF Customer Expectations Guide
questions.q: What is the 'golden rule' the guide gives customers for the first weeks?
options: Wash often to keep the film clean
Look at the car, don't touch the film
Wax it weekly to help curing
Park only in a humid garage
questions.why: "Look at the car. Don't touch the film." The biggest cause of avoidable problems is a customer pressing, picking or peeling something that would have settled. (3.2)

questions.handoutTitle: PPF Customer Expectations Guide
questions.q: When using a pressure washer on PPF, what does the guide advise?
options: Use a zero-degree nozzle close to edges for a deep clean
Hold it stationary on stubborn spots
Keep the nozzle 30–50 cm away, use a wide-fan nozzle, and never aim directly at an edge
Only ever use it on the film edges
questions.why: Keep the nozzle 30–50 cm back, use a wide-fan (40°) nozzle, never aim at an edge, and keep it moving. Misused pressure washers are the most common cause of avoidable lifting edges. (3.2 High-Pressure Washers)

questions.handoutTitle: PPF Customer Expectations Guide
questions.q: What realistic lifespan does the guide give for a modern, well-installed, well-cared-for PPF?
options: Around 7–10 years, sometimes longer
1–2 years
3–5 years
20+ years guaranteed
questions.why: Around 7–10 years, sometimes longer. End of life shows as gradual yellowing, loss of self-healing, or lifting edges — and UV (where the car is parked) is the biggest ageing factor. (3.2 Living With Your PPF)

questions.handoutTitle: Warranty and Guarantee — What You Promise, What the Law Promises
questions.q: How many distinct promises does the guide say every PPF job carries?
options: Two — the manufacturer's warranty and yours
Three — the manufacturer's warranty on the film, your guarantee on the workmanship, and the customer's statutory rights underneath both
One — whatever the invoice says
Four, one for each country
questions.why: Three promises stacked on each other. The manufacturer warrants the film; you guarantee your workmanship; and underneath both sit the customer's statutory rights, which are not voluntary and which no clause of yours removes. The customer sees one thing; the law sees three. (3.3 §2)

questions.handoutTitle: Warranty and Guarantee — What You Promise, What the Law Promises
questions.q: Under the UK Consumer Rights Act 2015, which section implies that a service must be performed with reasonable care and skill?
options: Section 50
Section 49
Section 54
Section 75
questions.why: Section 49 implies reasonable care and skill into every consumer service contract; section 50 makes what you said/wrote binding; remedies are in sections 54–56. (3.3 §3)

questions.handoutTitle: Warranty and Guarantee — What You Promise, What the Law Promises
questions.q: Can you contract out of CRA section 49 with a clause like 'no liability for installation defects'?
options: Yes, if the customer signs it
Yes, for B2B work only
No — such a clause is unenforceable against a private customer
Only if you offer a separate guarantee
questions.why: You cannot contract out of section 49. "No liability for installation defects" or "all sales final" is unenforceable against a private customer. (3.3 §7)

questions.handoutTitle: Warranty and Guarantee — What You Promise, What the Law Promises
questions.q: In Germany, the Netherlands and Belgium, how does the law classify a PPF fitting job?
options: A sale of goods, governed by Directive (EU) 2019/771
A contract for work — Werkvertrag, aanneming van werk, aanneming
A supply of services with no statutory floor
A consumer credit agreement
questions.why: Fitting film to a customer's car is a contract for work: Werkvertrag in Germany (§§ 631 and 633 BGB), aanneming van werk in the Netherlands (arts. 7:750 and 7:759 BW), aanneming in Belgium. You owe a finished result on the customer's own property. The United Kingdom is the exception and applies both its goods and its services chapters to the same job. (3.3 §3)

questions.handoutTitle: Warranty and Guarantee — What You Promise, What the Law Promises
questions.q: The "minimum two-year EU legal guarantee of conformity" comes from Directive (EU) 2019/771. When does it apply to what you do?
options: To every install you carry out in the EU
Only when a consumer buys goods from you — film sold over the counter without a fitting
Only to the manufacturer, never to you
Never, in any circumstances
questions.why: 2019/771 is the Sale of Goods Directive. It is real, and it applies when a consumer buys goods — including film you sell over the counter without fitting it. It is not the measure of your liability for an installation. If your terms say "two-year EU legal guarantee", that sentence is describing the wrong contract. (3.3 §3)

questions.handoutTitle: Warranty and Guarantee — What You Promise, What the Law Promises
questions.q: In the three contract-for-work countries, when does the burden of proof move from you to the customer?
options: Never — it stays with the installer for the life of the film
At the moment the customer accepts the finished job (Abnahme in Germany)
Six months after handover
When the manufacturer's warranty expires
questions.why: Up to acceptance you must show the work is free of defects; after acceptance the customer must show the defect exists and that it was there at handover. Whoever has to prove it usually loses, so handover is the event that decides most disputes. The United Kingdom splits it: a six-month presumption on the film, none at all on your workmanship. (3.3 §5)

questions.handoutTitle: Warranty and Guarantee — What You Promise, What the Law Promises
questions.q: Your terms advertise "a full two-year guarantee" which, read closely, covers exactly what the customer would have got from the law anyway. What is wrong with that?
options: Nothing — restating the customer's legal rights makes them clearer
Nothing, as long as you name the manufacturer's film warranty alongside it
It only becomes a problem if a customer complains to a regulator
It is a banned commercial practice — presenting statutory rights as a distinctive feature of your offer is prohibited outright, whether or not anyone was misled
questions.why: A commercial guarantee is defined in law as an undertaking in addition to statutory rights, so a "guarantee" that only restates them is not a guarantee at all, and advertising it as one is the offence. Point 10 of Annex I to Directive 2005/29/EC, transposed at art. 6:193g BW in the Netherlands and art. VI.100 WER in Belgium; in the United Kingdom the list has been Schedule 20 to the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 since 2025-04-06. Write yours so it plainly does more: a longer period, a wider list of covered defects, a free annual inspection. (3.3 §6)

questions.handoutTitle: Warranty and Guarantee — What You Promise, What the Law Promises
questions.q: The film on a customer's car yellows badly, well inside the manufacturer's warranty period. It is a material fault, not an installation fault. Who does the customer's legal claim run against?
options: You, the installer — you are the business they contracted with
The film manufacturer, because the fault is in their material
Whichever party the manufacturer's warranty document names
Nobody — a material fault falls outside consumer law
questions.why: The customer's statutory rights run against the business they contracted with, which is you. The manufacturer never sold them anything. That is true in all four countries however the film failed, so "take it up with the film company" is not an answer available to you anywhere. What you can then recover from your own supplier is a separate question, and 6.4 sets it out country by country. (3.3 §1)

questions.handoutTitle: Warranty Claims — Handling the Customer While You Wait
questions.q: A claim has been with the manufacturer for two weeks and there is no news. What do you send the customer?
options: Nothing — contacting them with no news wastes their time
A note saying you expect a decision to go their way shortly
A short written update: where the claim is, what you have done since the last one, and when the next update is due
A phone call asking them to be patient, with nothing put in writing
questions.why: The update with nothing in it is the habit that keeps customers through a claim. Three lines, in writing, so the customer stops wondering and you build the dated record 5.10 §2 asks for anyway. (3.4 §3)

questions.handoutTitle: Warranty Claims — Handling the Customer While You Wait
questions.q: At the first appointment, which promise is safe to make?
options: That you will contact them every week whether or not there is news
That the claim will be approved
That the manufacturer will decide within four weeks
That they will not be charged whatever the outcome
questions.why: The weekly update is a promise about your own behaviour, so it is entirely within your control. Every other reassurance in that conversation depends on somebody else. Promise the contact, never the answer. (3.4 §2, §4)

questions.handoutTitle: Warranty Claims — Handling the Customer While You Wait
questions.q: In Germany, a customer sets you a reasonable deadline to put a defect right. It expires while you are still waiting on the manufacturer. What may they do?
options: Nothing until the manufacturer has decided
Report you to the film manufacturer
Have the work done elsewhere, charge you the cost, and demand that money from you in advance
Cancel the contract and automatically recover the whole price
questions.why: § 637 BGB, with advance payment under § 637(3). The manufacturer's assessment is not a step in it — the deadline runs whether or not your supplier has replied, and waiting on them is no answer to the bill. (3.4 §6)

questions.handoutTitle: Warranty Claims — Handling the Customer While You Wait
questions.q: The marks follow the pattern you see from brush washes rather than a film defect. When do you tell the customer the claim may be refused?
options: After the refusal arrives, with the manufacturer's reasoning attached
Never — saying it out loud weakens the claim
Only if they ask you directly
At the first appointment, naming the reason, before the claim is submitted
questions.why: Ten uncomfortable minutes on day one beats six weeks of the customer expecting a free replacement followed by a refusal they did not see coming. Name the specific reason and say what the repair would cost. (3.4 §5)

questions.handoutTitle: Warranty Claims — Handling the Customer While You Wait
questions.q: The manufacturer refuses the claim, and the failure turns out to be your workmanship. What has the refusal actually decided?
options: That the customer pays for the rework
That the customer's claim now runs against the manufacturer instead
That you should quote the manufacturer's wording so the customer knows it is not your decision
Who reimburses you — not what you owe the customer, which you still owe
questions.why: A supplier's decision settles the money between you and them. The customer contracted with you, so their claim stays with you throughout. Deliver the outcome as your answer, not the manufacturer's. (3.4 §7, 3.3 §1)
